text:
sam: quick flag — noticed p95 regression on enterprise-priority routes after kernel-v2 roll last night, ~30ms increase :eyes:
jules: ugh. is that global or only high-seq routes?
sam: mostly high-priority routes with avg seq len > 800, KV hit rate also dropped ~6% for those requests. profiling points to different kernel path + smaller microbatch sizes.
tariq: can you paste the flame/trace?
sam: attaching snippet from the perf dump:
```
# perf snapshot (trimmed)
alloc_batch_time: 12.3ms
kernel_dispatch_v2: 41.6ms
kv_lookup_remote: 7.9ms
microbatch_wait: 9.7ms
p95_total: 184.2ms (prev 154.1ms)
```
maria: hmm looks like kernel_dispatch_v2 is the big delta. Did the allocator change token budget targets?
sam: we rolled kernel switch + new batcher policy that reduces per-request token budget for fairness, but it seems to starve enterprise-priority paths when seqs are long.
jules: hypothesis: dynamic token budgets by route/tier are too aggressive for enterprise-priority; microbatching causes more kernels to be invoked for same tokens -> overhead.
tariq: proposed experiment: increase token_budget_target for enterprise-priority from 2048 -> 3072, and enable KV prefetch heuristic for long prefixes. run canary 10% on us-west1.
maria: SGTM. expected tradeoff = slight cost increase but p95 drop. what metrics to watch?
tariq: watch p95, p99, avg microbatch size, KV hit rate, kernel_dispatch time, cpu/gpu utilization. Also track per-token cost.
sam: here's the draft rollout patch (canary):
```yaml
batcher:
  route_overrides:
    enterprise-priority:
      token_budget_target: 3072
      kv_prefetch: true
      max_microbatch_delay_ms: 6
```
jules: nice. add a quick kernel gating flag so we can revert kernel_v2 for the canary if dispatch time spikes: `kernel_version: auto` fallback to v1 on slow path.
maria: i'll wire dashboard tiles and alert rule: fire if p95 > baseline + 20ms or KV hit rate drops > 3% for 10m.
sam: deploy-bot: starting canary rollout to us-west1 10%
deploy-bot: canary started for rollout-id rlt-2026-03-18-01 :rocket:
tariq: running perf job to collect microbatch histograms and seq distribution against sample traces. will post results in 30m. :coffee:
infra-bot: note: GPU kernel 2 has known increased dispatch overhead when microbatches < 8 under some archs — see #internal-kernels-ops.
jules: if canary shows p95 improvement and no cost blowup, we should consider making token_budget_target adaptive by percentile: e.g., set target = max(ceil(P95_seq_len * 1.25), base) per route. reduces manual tuning.
maria: love that. add a metric to observe P95_seq_len by route.
sam: initial canary results (first 30m): p95 enterprise-priority dropped from +30ms to +6ms. KV hit rate up 4%. microbatch size avg increased from 5.1 -> 7.8. kernel_dispatch_v2 still slightly higher than v1 but offset by fewer kernel calls.
tariq: promising. cost estimate: ~3.8% token cost increase for that route under current workload.
jules: thumbs up if we promote to 50% canary and monitor for 2hrs. :thumbsup:
maria: promoting now. deploy-bot: scaling canary to 50% rollout-id rlt-2026-03-18-01
deploy-bot: promotion complete. keep eyes on p99 for tail regressions.
sam: thanks all. next action: tldr -> make token_budget_target adaptive by route percentile and add kernel fallback on slow dispatch. i'll open a follow-up RFC with perf numbers and cost/benefit.
jules: assign to sam + tariq for implementation, maria for observability.
maria: noted. i'll add alert thresholds and a dashboard panel for per-route microbatch size distribution.
tariq: leaving notes in #internal-kernels-ops: added script `batch_curator_analyze.py` to compute P95_seq_len and suggest token targets. run it with `python tools/batch_curator_analyze.py --route enterprise-priority --window 1h`.
sam: great. closing thread when RFC is up. :white_check_mark:
